_readme: Pre-loaded class history so the teacher dashboard is NOT EMPTY on demo day.
An empty dashboard looks broken even when it is working correctly.
seed.py creates synthetic students, gives them gaps and confirmed misconception
diagnoses in these proportions, then the live demo adds one more on top - so the
heatmap has a believable shape AND visibly increments when the student confirms.
Synthetic students are never named in any teacher view; teacher endpoints only
The proportions are deliberately uneven. A flat heatmap tells a teacher nothing
and looks generated; a long tail with two clear leaders looks like a real class
and gives the demo something to point at.
The uncertainty_flags below are questions a CSW2 student might plausibly ask
that the Django corpus genuinely does not cover -- neighbouring CS topics, not
absurd ones. A flag panel full of obviously silly questions makes the refusal
look easy; these make it look necessary.
_gap_counts_readme: Every slug here MUST be a prerequisite concept, because seed.py writes these
as Gap rows with detected_from='diagnostic'. A gap on a concept the corpus
cannot teach is a lesson that refuses.
The two long-tail entries were python-classes-objects and html-forms; both
were demoted out of the prerequisite set (see concepts.json) and are now the
two concepts the diagnostic actually tests in their place.

What is the time complexity of Dijkstra's algorithm with a binary heap?

reteach_units.title: Which side carries the foreign key
reteach_units.body: Start from the question 'how many can this row point at?' A post has exactly one author, so a post row can hold one author id in one column. An author has many posts, and a single column cannot hold many ids. The key therefore lives on the many side. Work through it by drawing two tables and asking students to write the id in by hand - the impossibility of fitting several ids in one cell is the whole argument, and it lands better drawn than stated.
